title: Occurrence, Preparation, and Properties of Carbonates
lead: The carbonates and hydrogen carbonates of the representative metals are prepared from carbon dioxide and an oxide or hydroxide, or by precipitation. Limestone that dissolves in water holding carbon dioxide shapes caves, stalactites and stalagmites, and carbonates and hydrogen carbonates react with acids in antacids and in baking powder.
objectives: Describe the preparation, properties, and uses of some representative metal carbonates
summary_html: The usual method for the preparation of the carbonates of the alkali and alkaline earth metals is by reaction of an oxide or hydroxide with carbon dioxide. Other carbonates form by precipitation. Metal carbonates or hydrogen carbonates such as limestone (CaCO3), the antacid Tums (CaCO3), and baking soda (NaHCO3) are common examples. Carbonates and hydrogen carbonates decompose in the presence of acids and most decompose on heating.

exercises.prompt: Carbon forms the ${\text{CO}}_{3}{}^{2−}$ ion, yet silicon does not form an analogous ${\text{SiO}}_{3}{}^{2−}$ ion. Why?

answer.solution: Suggested approach: draw the carbonate ion with its carbon–oxygen π bond, then compare the sizes of carbon and silicon atoms and recall how carbon dioxide and silicon dioxide differ in bonding; ask whether a silicon atom can form the π bond to oxygen that the carbonate ion needs.
